title: The V-style ski jump
hook: One ski jumper was marked down for his style, then everyone copied him.
peek: In the mid-1980s the Swedish ski jumper Jan Boklöv started spreading his skis in a V. Judges cut his style marks, but he flew so much farther that the whole sport switched to his technique within a few years.
lede: For decades, ski jumpers flew with their skis held tight and parallel. In the mid-1980s the Swede Jan Boklöv began opening the tips into a V. Judges, who award style points, saw a messy jump and marked him down. But the V turned his body and skis into a wing, and his distances kept beating everyone else's.

bullets.text: Ski jumping scores add distance points to style points from five judges. Boklöv lost style points for his V, but the extra distance more than made up for it.
In the 1988–89 season, Boklöv won the overall World Cup. Winning the sport's biggest season-long prize with a frowned-on technique made other jumpers take notice.
Wind tunnel tests and later studies showed the V gives more lift than parallel skis. Jumpers fly farther from the same hill, while lying flatter over the skis.
By the 1992 Winter Olympics in Albertville, nearly every top jumper used the V and the judges had stopped penalising it. The 16-year-old Finn Toni Nieminen won gold with it.
